status_summary: Executive Order 14169 (signed 2025-01-20) paused new obligations and disbursements of foreign development assistance for a 90-day review under guidelines set by the Secretary of State, with a Secretary of State waiver power, and a State cable of 2025-01-24 (25 STATE 6828, read in a court-record copy) paused new obligations of foreign assistance funded by or through State and USAID to the maximum extent permitted by law, directed stop-work orders on existing awards, held new solicitations and awards until approved by the Office of Foreign Assistance and set review milestones at 30, 85 and 180 days, with waivers including military financing for Israel and Egypt and emergency food aid; USAID issued a companion notice the same day for its program accounts, NPR reported the same day that a State memo ordered a stop to work on virtually all U.S.-funded aid programs, including those run by implementing partners, and the Secretary of State approved a waiver of the pause for life-saving humanitarian aid on 2025-01-28, per a State Department press statement of 2025-01-29. A presidential memorandum of 2025-01-20 froze federal civilian hiring government-wide, with exceptions including political appointments, and a 2025-07-07 memorandum extended it to 2025-10-15; no separate State freeze on Foreign Service recruiting was found, though Government Executive reported in March 2026 that State brought on nearly 100 new Foreign Service officers in 2025 while onboarding of Pickering and Rangel fellows was delayed. On 2025-03-10 the Secretary of State announced that the program review, which AP says was carried out by political appointees at State and DOGE teams, was ending, with about 5,200 of 6,200 USAID programs eliminated, and EO 14222 (2025-02-26) separately required agencies to review existing contracts and grants, prioritizing funds to foreign entities, and to record a justification for each payment, a government-wide step parallel to the Mandate's call to freeze contracts and payments. Courts limited the payment freeze: after the Supreme Court on 2025-03-05 declined to vacate a district court order on payment for completed work, the district court on 2025-03-10 enjoined giving effect to pause-related actions taken from 2025-01-20 to 2025-02-13, the D.C. Circuit later vacated the injunction's impoundment portion, and the case remains open (aid-restructuring results are covered in c09-01 and c09-02, and treaty review in c06-08).

timeline.event: Executive Order 14169 (90 FR 8619, published 2025-01-30) paused new obligations and disbursements of development assistance funds to foreign countries and to implementing organizations and contractors pending program reviews under guidelines set by the Secretary of State, with determinations due within 90 days with the Secretary's concurrence and a Secretary of State waiver power; it does not address hiring or treaties.

A presidential memorandum dated 2025-01-20 froze hiring of federal civilian employees government-wide and barred contracting outside the government to evade the freeze, with exceptions including national security, public safety, immigration enforcement and political appointments; it expires once the OMB workforce plan is issued and does not mention the State Department or the Foreign Service.

A State Department cable to embassies, reported by AP, barred new spending on nearly all foreign assistance, with exceptions for emergency food aid and military aid to Israel and Egypt, and set review standards within about a month and a review within three months to inform the Secretary's recommendations.

A State Department cable to all posts (25 STATE 6828), implementing EO 14169, paused new obligations of foreign assistance funded by or through State and USAID pending a review, barring obligations to the maximum extent permitted by law and directing stop-work orders on existing awards consistent with their terms; it held new solicitations and new awards or extensions until reviewed and approved by the Office of Foreign Assistance, set review milestones at 30, 85 and 180 days, and listed waivers, subject to further review, for military financing for Israel and Egypt, emergency food aid, temporary staff salaries, earlier or stop-work-related expenses under existing awards and exceptions approved by the Director of Foreign Assistance.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of State (court-record copy on storage.courtlistener.com)

timeline.event: USAID issued a companion notice implementing EO 14169: it paused new obligations and sub-obligations for program accounts (not operating expenses), told contracting and agreement officers to issue stop-work orders or suspensions and not to extend existing awards, held new awards and solicitations pending review, and listed waivers for emergency food aid, temporary contractor salaries, earlier or stop-work-related expenses under existing awards and exceptions approved by the Director of Foreign Assistance.

NPR reports an internal State Department memo signed by the Secretary of State ordering a stop to work on virtually all programs that rely on U.S. foreign assistance funding, including those run by implementing partners, with exemptions for aid to Israel and Egypt and emergency food aid, and a review to be finished within 85 days.

The Secretary of State approves a waiver of the foreign assistance pause so that existing life-saving humanitarian assistance can continue or resume temporarily, with no new contracts beyond limited exceptions (State press statement of 2025-01-29, copy hosted by globalsecurity.org). Guidance extending the waiver to HIV treatment and related costs is dated 2025-02-06 in this record; a State information memo applying the waiver to life-saving HIV services (copy hosted by UNAIDS) is dated 2025-02-01, so the two dates conflict.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of State (copy hosted by globalsecurity.org)

timeline.event: EO 14222 (90 FR 11095) directs agencies to log a written justification for each payment under covered discretionary contracts and grants and to review existing covered awards within 30 days, prioritizing educational institutions and foreign entities, and to terminate or modify them where appropriate; a government-wide step parallel to the Mandate's call to freeze contracts and payments.

The Supreme Court denied the government's application (No. 24A831) to vacate a district court order requiring payment for completed work, vacating the Chief Justice's administrative stay and directing the district court to clarify the government's obligations with due regard for feasibility; four justices dissented.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: The Secretary of State announced the review of USAID programs was ending, with about 5,200 of 6,200 programs eliminated and the rest to be run by State; AP reported that political appointees at State and DOGE teams carried out the review.

The district court issued a preliminary injunction against giving effect to the State guidance and pause-related actions taken from 2025-01-20 to 2025-02-13, including payment for work completed before 2025-02-13, and against unlawful impoundment of foreign aid (per the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse).
A new presidential memorandum extended the federal hiring freeze to 2025-10-15.

The D.C. Circuit (Global Health Council v. Trump, Nos. 25-5097 and 25-5098; Judges Henderson, Katsas and Pan, Judge Pan dissenting) vacated the preliminary injunction's impoundment portion, holding the grantees lacked an APA or ultra vires cause of action to enforce the Impoundment Control Act; the portion requiring payment for work completed between 2025-01-20 and 2025-02-13 was not appealed, and the opinion notes the government had paid substantially all amounts owed under it. An amending order of 2025-08-28 directed the mandate to issue. The case remains open.

The Supreme Court (No. 25A269) granted the government's application for a stay of the 2025-09-03 district court order as to funding subject to the 2025-08-28 rescission special message, pending the D.C. Circuit appeal and any certiorari petition; three justices dissented.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: Government Executive reported that State brought on nearly 100 new Foreign Service officers in 2025, that more than 50 Pickering and Rangel fellows were still awaiting onboarding, and that the 2026 fellowship application cycles were on hold.

title: Freeze foreign aid, payments and hiring at inauguration pending a political review
uncertainties: The January 2025 State cable (25 STATE 6828, dated 2025-01-24) was read on 2026-10-22 in a court-record copy hosted by storage.courtlistener.com (Exhibit A, Document 1-10, filed on 2025-02-10 in the D.D.C. case AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition v. Department of State, No. 1:25-cv-00400); no copy on a State Department host was opened, so the copy was not compared with an agency original, and the six pages of the exhibit were not reconciled with the five cable pages an external retrieval reported. In that copy paragraph 7 bars new obligations to the maximum extent permitted by law and directs stop-work orders consistent with the terms of each award, and paragraphs 8 and 9 hold new solicitations and new awards or extensions until the Office of Foreign Assistance reviews and approves them, which is a conditional hold rather than an absolute bar; the waivers in paragraph 12 are stated to be subject to further review. Whether the Secretary's review concluded as the cable contemplated is covered by other records. A USAID notice of 2025-01-24 opened on USAID's GovDelivery account agrees with the cable on the pause, stop-work orders and the hold on new awards; the 2025-01-28 humanitarian waiver itself was not opened, only the State press statement announcing it. The stop-work date rests on an NPR report of 2025-01-24 and the waiver date on a State Department press statement of 2025-01-29 (copy hosted by globalsecurity.org; the state.gov page could not be fetched). The 2025-02-06 date for guidance extending the waiver to HIV treatment was earlier taken from Human Rights Watch, an advocacy group, and is an unverified lead at low confidence; the opened State information memo on life-saving HIV services under the waiver (copy hosted by UNAIDS) is dated 2025-02-01, and that date is the one an official document supports. The 2025-03-10 date of the review announcement is taken from same-day AP syndications; the ABC copy cited gives only a weekday. The D.C. Circuit opinion of 2025-08-13 and the Supreme Court dockets 24A831 and 25A269 were read; the 2025-03-10 district court injunction rests on the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse summary (docket updated 2026-02-21), not on the order. The D.C. Circuit opinion states that the unappealed payment-for-completed-work portion was substantially paid. No State-specific freeze on contracts beyond foreign aid, or on Foreign Service recruiting, was found. Partial overlap with c09-01 (the same 90-day pause as the first step of the USAID restructuring) and c09-02 (aid cuts) is a cross-reference, not a duplicate: this record tracks the Mandate's separate chapter 6 call (page 174) for an across-the-board freeze at inauguration, including hiring and contracts, pending political review. The c06-08 record on treaty review was not opened in this review. The hiring memorandum of 2025-01-20 expires on issue of the OMB workforce plan, so the 2025-07-07 extension to 2025-10-15 was not re-read here; the hiring freeze's end after 2025-10-15 was not checked. Independent review of 2026-10-16: the first 2025-01-20 timeline entry repeated the hiring-memorandum text under the EO 14169 link and was rewritten to describe EO 14169. The Supreme Court docket for No. 25A269 shows no entry after 2025-09-26, and the case-tracking page lists no court event after that date.
